thread:
maya: Heads up — after the routing tweak this morning I'm seeing a weird divergence: p50 for /v1/generate dropped ~25% but p95 increased ~40% in the last hour. dashboard link: https://console/redwood/d/latency
chris: Huh. Which aggregation are you looking at? endpoint-level or route-rollup?
maya: endpoint-level, region=us-west. I checked both raw and rollup. Raw endpoint medians look better but tail is worse.
chris: can you paste the query you used?
maya: sure — pasted below
```sql
-- simplified
SELECT percentile(0.50, latency_ms) AS p50,
       percentile(0.95, latency_ms) AS p95,
       count(*) AS samples
FROM request_latency
WHERE endpoint = '/v1/generate' AND ts > now() - interval '1 hour'
GROUP BY region, endpoint;
```
maya: counts are stable, ~12k samples in us-west.
deploy-bot: rollout: routing-policy v3 -> deployed to us-west at 06:12 UTC :white_check_mark:
alana: possible hypothesis: we introduced synthetic warmup traffic to the new fallback route and its latencies are concentrated around p50 (fast), which pulls the endpoint median down but the real customer traffic still sits in the tail. did we tag synthetic samples correctly?
maya: checked tags — synthetic=true for the warmup job. dashboard rollup filters should drop synthetic but I see some synthetic samples in the endpoint view.
chris: if some synthetic samples are slipping into the endpoint enumeration they could bias quantiles if the dashboard merges per-region summaries incorrectly. how do we merge percentiles today?
sre-jen: merging approach: we store per-shard t-digests, then merge digests on read. weighting is by sample_count per shard. bug risk if sample_count is wrong or if we normalized weights twice.
maya: I dug into the backend logs: when we reconciled route aliases we created an alias entry with sample_count=0 for the fallback route for a short window (race). those 0-count shards were still included in the merge list.
chris: oh. If we include a digest with sample_count=0 the merge logic currently treats missing counts as 1 (legacy) — that would underweight big shards and accidentally amplify small-but-fast synthetic shards.
chris: quick proof-of-concept locally: merge with a 0-count digest + small fast digest -> p50 drops, p95 jumps.
maya: screenshot attached (small).
alana: nice catch. two follow-ups: 1) patch the merge to ignore digests with sample_count<=0, 2) add an assertion in ingestion to never create alias shards with zero count.
sre-jen: agree. also add a dashboard annotation that marks when routing-policy rollouts include warmup traffic so we can correlate.
chris: I'll open a PR to change merge behaviour (short patch) and add a unit test. want me to revert the recent dashboard change meanwhile? it flipped rollup mode from "raw-sampled" to "per-region-merge" which exacerbated the artifact.
maya: yes please revert to raw-sampled for the impacted panel until we confirm the merge fix.
deploy-bot: revert: dashboard panel 8 -> raw-sampled (manual rollback) at 06:54 UTC :arrows_counterclockwise:
alana: I'll add an eval job to run synthetic warmup but tag with synthetic=true and have the console surface synthetic-sample-rate as a chart.
sre-jen: Action items:
- chris: PR for safe-merge + test (ETA 2h)
- maya: collect sample_ids for the spike window and paste into issue
- alana: dashboard annotation + synthetic-rate chart (ETA EOD)
- ops: ensure warmup job tags are enforced (follow up with infra)
chris: created issue #10842 and linked the PR in the thread draft. assigning to @chris for PR review.
maya: thanks. gonna watch p95 over next 30m and confirm revert helped. :eyes:
chris: quick note — if anyone wants to reproduce locally: run the merge harness with these two t-digests (attached) and compare percentile outputs.
maya: confirmed after revert p50 and p95 look consistent again (small window). will update issue with before/after charts. :thumbsup:
